word:greek-nt:G0029.explanation: Angareuo means to compel someone to go. For example, Simon is compelled to go and carry a cross.

word:greek-nt:G0076.explanation: Adam is the name of the first man.

word:greek-nt:G0155.explanation: Aitēma means a petition or request.

word:greek-nt:G0353.explanation: Analambanō means to take up or raise. It can also mean to take someone aboard.

word:greek-nt:G0461.explanation: Anorthoō means to make something upright or straight again. It can also mean to restore or set up again after something has fallen.

word:greek-nt:G0564.explanation: This word describes someone who is uncircumcised—someone who has not received circumcision. It functions as a descriptive term identifying the absence of this physical mark. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 7:51. The word’s basic meaning is straightforward, while its force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and the way the speaker applies the description there.

word:greek-nt:G0586.explanation: Apodekatoō means to take off or deduct a tenth. It also means to give a tenth, or to tithe.

word:greek-nt:G0605.explanation: This word means “restoration,” referring to the act of bringing something back to its proper or former condition. It describes renewal or return rather than simple continuation. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 3:21. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea remains restoration: something being returned or renewed according to what it should be.

word:greek-nt:G0748.explanation: Archieratikos means high-priestly, describing what belongs to the high priest.

word:greek-nt:G1141.explanation: This word means “demonic” or “of the devil.” It describes something associated with demonic powers or the devil, identifying its source or character rather than presenting it as coming from God. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in James 3:15. Its precise force in that verse is understood from the surrounding passage, but the word itself points to what is demonic or devilish. The Bible’s use here gives this adjective a clear negative identification: it marks something as belonging to the realm of the devil.

word:greek-nt:G1273.explanation: Dianyktereuō means to spend the whole night.

word:greek-nt:G1387.explanation: Dolioō means to act deceitfully, deceive, or use fraud.

word:greek-nt:G1556.explanation: Ekdikeō means to avenge or defend. A widow uses it to ask for defense from her adversary.

word:greek-nt:G1732.explanation: Endeixis means a showing, proof, or demonstration. It can also mean a sign or token serving as proof.

word:greek-nt:G1747.explanation: Enedra means an ambush. It can also refer to a plot against someone.

word:greek-nt:G1813.explanation: Exaleiphō means to wipe away, blot out, or erase. It describes sins being blotted out and tears being wiped away.

word:greek-nt:G1938.explanation: Epithumētēs means someone who eagerly desires. Here, the desire is directed toward evil things.

word:greek-nt:G2045.explanation: ἐραυνῶν means to search diligently or examine.

word:greek-nt:G2117.explanation: Euthus means straight, describing a direction that is not crooked.

word:greek-nt:G2188.explanation: “Ephphatha!” means “open!” It is a direct command calling for something to be opened. This Greek New Testament word is preserved as a spoken expression rather than commonly translated into an ordinary English sentence. It occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at Mark 7:34. The word’s basic meaning is therefore concise and forceful: an instruction to open. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and the person or thing being addressed.

word:greek-nt:G2221.explanation: Zōgreō means to capture alive or take captive.

word:greek-nt:G2283.explanation: Thamar is a personal name for Tamar. Tamar is identified as the mother of Perez and Zerah by Judah.

word:greek-nt:G2324.explanation: This word means “servant”: a person who serves another and carries out an assigned role. It presents someone in terms of service rather than independence or personal status. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs only once, in Hebrews 3:5. The word itself identifies a servant, while the surrounding verse and passage determine the particular responsibility or comparison intended there. Its basic meaning remains focused on faithful service and a subordinate role. [p03:word:greek-nt:G2324:identity] [p03:word:greek-nt:G2324:occurrences] [p01:word:greek-nt:G2324:reference:0]

word:greek-nt:G2474.explanation: Israel is the name given to Jacob and also the name of the people of God.

word:greek-nt:G2496.explanation: Iōram is a personal name, rendered Joram.

word:greek-nt:G2540.explanation: Kairos means a time or season. It may describe the time before another event, as well as times whose signs are discerned.

word:greek-nt:G2643.explanation: “Reconciliation” means the restoration of a relationship from separation or opposition to peace and fellowship. It is a noun describing this restored condition or the bringing of parties back together. In the Greek New Testament, the word appears four times, in Romans and 2 Corinthians, and is consistently rendered “reconciliation.” Its precise emphasis in any verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea is restored relationship rather than continued estrangement.

word:greek-nt:G2706.explanation: Kataphroneō means to despise or scorn—to treat someone or something with contempt or disregard.

word:greek-nt:G2759.explanation: Kentron means a sting. It can also mean a goad.

word:greek-nt:G2801.explanation: Klasma means a fragment or broken piece.

word:greek-nt:G3060.explanation: Loidoros means a railer, reviler, or slanderer.

word:greek-nt:G3114.explanation: Makrothumeo means to be patient or to endure for a long time. It describes staying patient while waiting, like a farmer waiting for his crop.

word:greek-nt:G3392.explanation: Miainō means to stain, pollute, defile, or corrupt. It can describe flesh being defiled.

word:greek-nt:G3622.explanation: Oikonomia means management, administration, or stewardship of affairs. In one setting, that stewardship is entrusted to a person.

word:greek-nt:G3657.explanation: Homilia means companionship. It can also refer to conversation.

word:greek-nt:G3730.explanation: Hormē means a violent assault or an impulse.

word:greek-nt:G3785.explanation: Ophelon expresses a wish—“I wish” or “Would that”—for something desired.

word:greek-nt:G3819.explanation: Palai means long ago, of old, or in times past.

word:greek-nt:G3846.explanation: Paraballō means to arrive or reach a place after traveling.

word:greek-nt:G3903.explanation: Paraskeuazō means to prepare or make preparations.

word:greek-nt:G4036.explanation: Perilypos means very sorrowful or greatly grieved.

word:greek-nt:G4069.explanation: Persis is a personal name, referring to a woman named Persis. It does not function as a description, action, or general spiritual term, but identifies an individual. In the Greek New Testament, the name appears once, in Romans 16:12. The available wording preserves it as “Persis,” so no broader meaning or alternate definition should be added. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and the way Paul refers to her there.

word:greek-nt:G4115.explanation: Platyno means to enlarge or make broad. It can also mean to open wide.

word:greek-nt:G4230.explanation: Pragmateia means an affair or business matter.

word:greek-nt:G4285.explanation: Proēgeomai means to prefer or put above.

word:greek-nt:G4322.explanation: Prosanaplēroō means to fill up by adding to, or to supply what is lacking.

word:greek-nt:G4357.explanation: Prosmenō means to remain, abide, persist, or adhere to something.

word:greek-nt:G4414.explanation: This word describes a ringleader—a person recognized as the leading figure among a group, especially in an accusation or charge. It points to someone viewed as directing, influencing, or standing at the forefront of others, rather than merely being one participant. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 24:5. The precise force of the word in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central meaning is a person regarded as the group’s chief leader.

word:greek-nt:G4560.explanation: Sarkinos means fleshly or carnal. It can describe something consisting of flesh, as in fleshy tables of the heart.

word:greek-nt:G4692.explanation: Speudo means to hasten or hurry. It can also mean to desire earnestly.

word:greek-nt:G4771.explanation: Sy means you. It can identify the people being addressed, as in “all of you,” or show that something is directed to them, as in “to you.”

word:greek-nt:G4872.explanation: Synanabainō means to go up with.

word:greek-nt:G4898.explanation: This word means a companion or traveling companion—someone who journeys alongside another person. It describes a fellow traveler rather than merely someone associated from a distance. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice: once in Acts and once in 2 Corinthians. Its basic sense remains focused on shared travel and companionship, while the surrounding passage determines the particular role that person has in each reference.

word:greek-nt:G4951.explanation: Syro means to draw, drag, or force away.

word:greek-nt:G5044.explanation: This word means “to bring up children” or “to raise children.” It describes the work of caring for children as they grow, including the ongoing responsibility of bringing them up. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in 1 Timothy 5:10. Its basic sense points to child-rearing rather than merely giving birth, emphasizing the practical care and upbringing involved. The surrounding passage determines how this responsibility fits the particular situation, but the word itself focuses on raising children.

word:greek-nt:G5181.explanation: Tyrannus is the name of an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.

word:greek-nt:G5202.explanation: Hydropoteō means to drink only water.

word:greek-nt:G5350.explanation: Phthengomai means to speak aloud or utter.

word:greek-nt:G5431.explanation: Phrontizō means to be thoughtful, careful, or to give heed.

word:greek-nt:G5493.explanation: This word refers to a brook or valley—a natural channel or low place in the land. It names a physical feature of the landscape rather than an action, quality, or person. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, at John 18:1, so its broader range of use cannot be established from repeated examples. Its basic sense remains a brook or valley, with the surrounding verse determining which aspect of that meaning is intended there.

word:greek-nt:G5552.explanation: Chrysous means golden—made of gold or adorned with gold.
